steps.do: Create the src folder if it is missing.
In src/styles.css, add the line @import tailwindcss at the top, then add an @theme block with --color-brand-600: #2563eb and --font-sans set to a system font stack.

steps.do: Create the components folder if it is missing.
In src/components/Button.tsx, set the base class string to inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md font-medium text-sm leading-5 tracking-normal.
List the typography utilities in the file so there are exactly four matches.

Confirm the text-sm token resolves to a 0.875rem font size and a 1.25rem line height.

K-022007.check: rg prints exactly 4 lines and tsc exits 0 with no output.

Writing text-[14px] skips the type scale and drifts from other components.
Put color classes in the variants, not the base string.

steps.do: In src/components/Button.tsx, define a size map where sm is h-8 px-3 text-xs, md is h-10 px-4 text-sm min-h-11, and lg is h-12 px-6 text-base min-h-11.
Count the size keys in the map so the result is three.
Confirm no size uses an arbitrary height value.
Lint the component file.
Confirm min-h-11 resolves to 2.75rem, which is 44px at the default root size of 16px.

K-022008.example: The md size combines h-10 with min-h-11, and min-height wins over height, so the rendered button is 44px tall. The arbitrary-height count prints 0 and eslint exits 0.
K-022008.check: rg prints 3, the arbitrary-height count prints 0, and eslint exits 0 with no errors.

Do not use h-[44px] since it skips the spacing scale and cannot be themed.
A small model may miss a size key, so count the keys and confirm lg is present.

steps.do: In src/components/Button.tsx, add focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-brand-600 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 to the base class string.
Count the focus ring utility so it appears exactly once.
Build the stylesheet so the ring utilities are generated.
Confirm the generated CSS includes the focus-visible selector.
Check the ring color against the page background, which must reach 3:1.

K-022009.example: brand-600 #2563eb on white is about 5.2:1, which passes the 3:1 rule for non-text indicators. The rg count prints 1 and grep prints 1 or more.
K-022009.check: rg prints 1, grep prints 1 or more, and the build exits 0.

The ring offset defaults to white, so on a dark page it needs its own color class.

steps.do: Create the scripts folder if it is missing.
Write scripts/contrast.mjs with a WCAG relativeLuminance function and pairs for white on #2563eb and white on #1e40af.
Run the script and read the ratio printed for each pair.
Confirm each printed ratio is at least 4.5 for normal button text.

K-022010.example: White text on #2563eb gives 5.17:1, which passes the 4.5:1 rule for text, and on #1e40af it gives 8.72:1. The script prints PASS on both lines.
K-022010.check: The node command prints two lines, primary 5.17:1 PASS and strong 8.72:1 PASS, and exits 0.
traps: WCAG contrast uses linearized sRGB channels, not raw 0 to 255 values.
A small model may compare hex digits directly and report a wrong ratio.
Large text passes at 3:1, but button labels are normal text and need 4.5:1.

steps.do: Find every arbitrary text, font, or tracking class in the Button file with line numbers.
Replace each arbitrary value with the nearest scale class, such as text-[14px] becoming text-sm and text-[16px] becoming text-base.
Recount the arbitrary classes so the result is zero.
Rebuild the stylesheet to confirm the replaced classes still compile.

K-022011.example: text-[14px] becomes text-sm, which is 0.875rem and 14px, so the rendered size does not change. The recount command prints 0 after the edits.
K-022011.check: rg -c prints 0 and the build exits 0.
traps: A small model may map 15px to text-sm, which changes the size, so pick the nearest token deliberately.
Editing the lines without rerunning the count leaves the result unverified.
Do not add new arbitrary values while fixing old ones.

steps.do: Confirm the card stylesheet contains a prefers-reduced-motion media query.
Run the Playwright test that calls page.emulateMedia with reducedMotion set to reduce, then checks the card transition duration.
Confirm the Playwright output reports 1 passed and no failures.

K-022012.example: Inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), the .card rule sets transition-duration to 0.01ms and animation to none. The spec expects getComputedStyle on the card to return transitionDuration of 0.00001s when reduced motion is emulated.
K-022012.check: grep prints a line number with prefers-reduced-motion, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models write the media query but forget to override the animation property itself.
Setting transition to none on the base rule removes motion for every user, not only those with reduced motion.

steps.do: List every transition declaration in the card stylesheet.
Search for any transition duration of 300ms or more, or of 1000ms or more.
Run the timing spec that reads transitionDuration from computed style on .card:hover.
Confirm the spec reports a measured duration of 0.2s or less.

K-022013.example: The rule .card with transition: transform 0.2s ease passes the search because no match is printed. The spec reads transitionDuration as 0.2s on hover and the assertion expects a value at most 0.2s.
K-022013.check: The rg search prints no lines and the Playwright run prints '1 passed' with duration 0.2s or less.
traps: Small models miss durations written in seconds, such as 0.5s, because the search only checks ms values. Search for s values too.
A transition declared on the base rule but overridden on hover can hide a slow value, so check both states.

steps.do: Search the card stylesheet for transitions on layout properties such as width, height, top, left, or margin.
Count the transition lines that name transform or opacity.
Run the layout spec that compares card bounding box width and height before and after hover.
Confirm the layout spec reports a width and height change of 0px.

K-022014.example: The search for width, height, top, left, or margin in transition lines prints nothing. The count command prints 2 because the card has one transform transition and one opacity transition.
K-022014.check: The rg search prints no lines, the grep count prints 2 or more, and the Playwright run prints '1 passed' with a 0px size change.
traps: Small models assume transform and opacity are the only animated properties, but a shorthand like transition: all can animate layout. Search for all as well.
Counting transition lines does not prove the values are correct, so run the Playwright check too.

steps.do: Search the card stylesheet for infinite animation iteration counts.
Confirm any line that prints is inside the reduced-motion media query, or that nothing prints at all.
Run the idle spec that waits 2 seconds after load and calls document.getAnimations to count running animations.
Confirm the idle spec reports 1 passed with an animation count of 0.

K-022015.example: A shimmer rule with animation-iteration-count set to infinite fails the check unless it sits inside the reduced-motion block. The idle spec expects document.getAnimations().length to equal 0 after 2000ms.
K-022015.check: The grep prints no lines outside the reduced-motion block, and Playwright prints '1 passed' with an animation count of 0.
traps: Small models forget that the animation shorthand can hide infinite inside it, so search for animation as well.
A count of 0 right after load can be misleading, so the wait of 2 seconds matters.

steps.do: List every translateY declaration in the card stylesheet.
Search for a lift larger than 4px, meaning translateY with a negative value of 5px or more.
Run the lift spec that reads the card bounding box top before and after hover.
Confirm the reported top change is exactly 4px.

K-022016.example: The hover rule sets transform to translateY(-4px) on .card:hover. The lift spec expects the card top coordinate to drop by exactly 4px after hover.
K-022016.check: The large-lift search prints no lines, and Playwright prints '1 passed' with a top change of 4px.
traps: Small models pick a lift value like -8px and forget the design limit of 4px. Check the number in the stylesheet, not the intent.
Bounding box checks can be off by subpixel values, so compare with a tolerance of 0.5px if the test rounds.

steps.do: Confirm the card stylesheet declares a transition property.
Run the transitionend spec that attaches a listener, hovers the card, and records performance.now at the event.
Confirm the logged elapsed time is 300ms or less.
Confirm the logged transitionend count is exactly 1.

K-022017.example: The spec hovers the card and logs an elapsed time of 210ms with an event count of 1. The transition declared as transform 0.2s ease causes one transitionend event for the transform property.
K-022017.check: The grep prints the transition line, and Playwright prints '1 passed' with elapsed time at most 300ms and count 1.
traps: Small models count one transitionend per property, so a card with transform and opacity fires two events. Count per property, and expect 2 when both change.
Adding a listener after hover misses the event entirely, so attach it before the hover action.

K-022018.check: grep -c '^|' prints 8. grep -c Esc prints 1. grep -n prints one Tab row with its line number.

Do not bind Esc to two actions, because Esc must always cancel.

Confirm the error wrapper sets role alert in the source.
Run axe against the error route limited to WCAG 2.1 AA rules.
Check that text-red-700 on bg-red-50 has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, which is 5.92:1 for these values.

Build the stylesheet with the Tailwind CLI into dist.
Count how many times the error background class appears in the built CSS.
Count how many times the empty text color class appears in the built CSS.

Find existing responsive md: classes in the nav components to match.

steps.do: Check whether the forms plugin is already installed.
Check which Tailwind version is pinned in the project.
Confirm the CSS entry file that will hold the plugin line exists.

Record in the plan that a v3 project loads it in the plugins array of tailwind.config.js.

steps.do: Count the planned field entries in the plan file and record the total.
Create the directory for the end-to-end tests.
Create the empty test file for nav validation.
Set the pass rule as zero axe violations and at most 200ms from invalid submit to visible error text.
Confirm the Playwright tool is available to run the spec.

K-022028.check: grep -c prints a number such as 4, and npx playwright --version prints a version such as Version 1.48.0.

steps.do: Create the tests directory that will hold the performance test file.
Write tests/test_input_perf.py with an async test that uses app.run_test() and awaits pilot.press() once per character.
Wrap each press in time.perf_counter() calls and record the gap in milliseconds in a list.
Sort the list and assert that the 95th percentile value is below 50.0 ms, printing the value.
Run the test file in quiet mode to get the pass or fail result and the printed p95 line.

K-022029.example: Typing a 200-character string through pilot.press must keep the p95 keystroke gap under 50.0 ms. The test prints the p95 value so pytest -s shows the measured number.
K-022029.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and the printed p95 value is below 50.0 ms.
traps: Do not time pilot.press without awaiting it, because the timer then measures only coroutine creation.
Do not read Input.value before await pilot.pause(), or the value may lag behind the last key.

steps.do: Search the app source for any recompose call that a change handler might trigger.
Count the compose definitions in the source to confirm there is exactly one screen compose method.
Add a class-level counter that the screen compose method increments each time it runs.
Write a test that presses 200 characters through pilot.press and then asserts the counter equals 1.
Run only the compose count test by name.

K-022030.example: After 200 keypresses the compose counter should read 1, the value from startup, instead of 201. Any value above 1 means an Input handler is calling self.recompose().
K-022030.check: rg finds no recompose call inside the Input change handler, and pytest prints '1 passed' for compose_count.
traps: Small models often count Input widget instances instead of the screen compose method, which tests nothing useful.
Do not count the initial mount twice; the counter should start at zero before the app runs.

steps.do: Build a 10,000-character string in the test file by repeating a single letter.
Assign the string to Input.value inside an async run_test block and time that assignment with time.perf_counter().
Assert that the elapsed time is below 100 ms and that len(input.value) equals 10000.
Run the paste test with the durations table printed so the timing is visible.
Run the length check on its own to confirm all characters arrived.

K-022031.example: The test assigns 10000 copies of the letter a to Input.value and asserts the elapsed time is under 100 ms. A length check of 10000 confirms no characters were dropped during the assignment.
K-022031.check: pytest reports 2 passed and the durations table lists the paste test below 0.100s.
traps: Assigning value fires Changed events, so do not loop over characters and assign one at a time.
A length of 10001 means the string generator is off by one, not that the widget is wrong.

steps.do: Check that Cargo.toml lists ratatui as a dependency before writing any test.
Create the tests directory for the integration test file.
Write tests/input_render.rs with a test that builds Terminal::new(TestBackend::new(80, 24)) outside the timed section.
Inside the test, call terminal.draw 1000 times in a loop and time the loop with std::time::Instant.
Assert the average per frame is under 1 millisecond and print it.
Run the test in release mode so the timing reflects real builds.

K-022032.example: Drawing an Input paragraph 1000 times into an 80x24 TestBackend must average under 1.000 ms per draw. The printed average shows the measured number in the test output.
K-022032.check: cargo prints 'test input_draw_budget ... ok' and the printed average is below 1.000 ms.
traps: Running without --release gives timings that do not match what users see, so always use the flag.
Do not construct the Terminal inside the timed loop, since that adds setup cost to the draw number.

steps.do: Find where the Paragraph that draws the Input is created so the test targets the right code.
Write a test that draws the Input once, then draws again after adding one character to its value.
Compare the two buffers with Buffer::diff and count the returned update entries.
Assert that the count is 3 or fewer changed cells.
Run the diff test by name with output shown.

K-022033.example: After typing the letter a into an empty 40-column Input, Buffer::diff should return at most 3 updates: the typed glyph and up to two cursor cells. The test prints the count so the number is visible in the output.
K-022033.check: cargo prints 'test typing_one_char_diff ... ok' and the printed update count is 3 or less.
traps: Buffer::diff returns a list of changed positions, so count the list entries rather than adding up cell widths.
Comparing two buffers from the same draw gives zero changes, so draw once before the keystroke.

steps.do: Search the test folder for time.sleep calls, since they hide real latency and must not be used as timing.
Run the Input test file with a 2-second timeout applied to each test.
Print the five slowest tests and confirm none of them takes longer than 0.5 seconds.

K-022034.example: Every test in tests/test_input_perf.py must finish within 2 seconds, and --durations=5 lists any test above 0.5s for review. A sleep call found by rg in the tests means that test measures a delay instead of the widget.
K-022034.check: pytest prints passed for every test with exit code 0, and the durations table shows no entry above 0.500s.
traps: The --timeout flag needs the pytest-timeout plugin installed, otherwise pytest rejects the option.
Do not replace a timing assertion with time.sleep, since that adds delay and proves nothing about the widget.

steps.do: Find the empty-state wrapper div in src/components/Card.tsx by searching for its text.
Add data-testid='card-empty' to the empty-state wrapper div found in the previous step.
Create the spec file tests/card.spec.ts, then write a Playwright test that renders the card with items set to an empty array and checks the wrapper is visible.
Run only the empty-state Playwright test by matching its name.
Confirm the runner reports one passed test and zero failed tests. If it reports 0 passed, the grep matched no test.

K-022035.example: The empty wrapper uses the classes 'flex flex-col items-center gap-2 p-6 text-center text-gray-500' and holds the text 'No projects yet' and a button 'Create project'. The spec asserts getByTestId('card-empty') is visible and contains 'No projects yet'.
K-022035.check: Output shows '1 passed' and exit code 0; '0 passed' means the grep matched no test.
traps: Small models often omit the data-testid, so the locator finds nothing and the test times out.
Passing undefined instead of an empty array can make the test pass for the wrong reason.
A test that never runs is not evidence, so read the pass count.

Record the choice aria-invalid:border-red-700 for an input that sets aria-invalid from component state.
